note: Which ground plate each duty stands on, and how each plate is drawn. Read by tools/ui_debug/generate_placement_sheet.py and generate_duty_sow.py. The plates themselves live in ui/assets-gothic/grounds/ and are DISCOVERED -- what art exists is a fact about the folder, so nothing here lists them. What is decided, and therefore written down, is which duty gets which, and how each one is toned down to sit under sculpts rather than compete with them.
layer_note: A ground is a layer, not a tile face. The duty-tiles tree holds the opaque face of the wheel; a plate is a transparent cut-out drawn ON TOP of that face and UNDER the figures, so the same plate can sit on any face and a face can change without redrawing its ground.
by_duty_note: Keyed by duty slug rather than by compass position, because duty tiles can be shuffled by a scenario and a ground belongs to the duty rather than to the place it happens to sit this game. Assigned in the placement sheet's wheel view and saved from it; the sow plays on the result. Both pages resolve a duty to its plate through dutyGroundFor() in tools/ui_debug/duty_sculpt_rules.js, so there is no second answer to drift from this one.

camera.why: its own outline cannot give a camera and its measuring ring can. ground_ellipse fits an ellipse; this plate is a ragged patch of plank ends, and the fit visibly misses -- it bulges past the timber on one side and falls inside it on the other, reading 30.66. The ring drawn on the source image IS a circle and fits at 31.14. The two agree to 0.48, inside the 1.5 agreement bar, so the plate is sound and the ring is the better of its two numbers. FIRST RECORDED AT 31.57 AND CORRECTED THE SAME DAY: that came from filling the ring and taking its bounding box, which measures the ring's OUTER edge and so reports a steeper camera than the ring was drawn at. Measured against rings of known centreline the old method erred by up to +0.70 degrees, more than the whole tolerance a plate is held to. The ring was stripped when the art was filed, so this cannot be re-derived from the committed PNG -- which is the whole reason it is written down here
camera.method: least-squares ellipse fit to the ring's pixels

grounds_note: All whole-number percentages. `anchor` is where down the plate's own ink the standing line falls -- where the figures' feet belong -- and it is per plate rather than global because it is a property of the picture: measured at the widest row the round rimmed plates all sit near 48%. Two plates have ever differed and both for the same reason: flagstones_slab read 61% while it was a ragged patch of loose slabs with no rim, and came back to 47.9% the day it was redrawn as a round rimmed plate; cobbles_oval reads 57.8% as of 2026-09-23 and is a ragged patch with no rim BY DESIGN. A rim is most of what sits below the equator, so a plate without one has less ink under its widest row and its anchor rises. A value far from 48 means a plate is not the same kind of object as the rest, not that it is tuned differently -- and for cobbles_oval that is the intent rather than a fault. `scale` is the plate's width as a percentage of the frame's. `dim`, `saturate` and `opacity` tone it down; the plates arrive at full strength and compete with the sculpts until they are brought down.
angle_note:
SETTLED AT 32 DEGREES, and the assignments follow it. Every duty now stands on flagstones_grey (31.5) or limestone_irregular (31.9), the two plates drawn at the board's camera; the sculpts on file measure 32.2, 32.3 and 33.5. Ground and figure are within about a degree and a half of each other, which is inside the scatter of the generator itself.

ALL FIVE PLATES NOW PASS. slate_irregular and flagstones_slab were redrawn on 2026-09-23 and read 31.1 and 32.0; cobbles_oval was redrawn the same day and reads 31.6, where the plate it replaced sat at 39.8 and had been kept as the evidence of what a mismatch looks like. That plate is now at candidates/cobbles_oval_c01.png.

THE WINDOW IS LOCKED: target 31.55, tolerance 0.48, so 31.07 to 32.03. Constants, not a formula over this folder -- a plate outside them fails rather than widening them.

They were derived once, on 2026-09-23, from the six plates then on file, every one of which had been looked at under figures and kept: slate_irregular 31.07, planks_rough 31.14, flagstones_grey 31.52, cobbles_oval 31.63, limestone_irregular 31.89, flagstones_slab 32.02 -- mean 31.55, largest deviation 0.48. That replaced a target of 32.0 and a tolerance of 1.0, both picked rather than measured, and which the set never centred on: five of the six sat below 32. It is about half as wide, deliberately -- against the batch that produced the current cobbles plate it admits exactly the one chosen by eye.

FOR A FEW HOURS THE WINDOW WAS THE FORMULA, recomputed from the folder, and that was wrong: a specification defined by the thing it judges has no fixed point. Simulated, filing eight plates each landing on the current ceiling moves the target +0.54 and the ceiling +1.09, every step legitimate and every suite green. Worse and less visible, filing the BEST of each batch over twelve plates walks the target DOWN from 31.55 to 31.43 while the ceiling stays pinned at 32.02 -- the highest plate anchors the top, so everything new lands below the mean and widens the window downward. The set drifts away from the sculpts one plate at a time while every step looks like tightening the standard. The tolerance was also set by a single plate, whichever sat furthest out.

So changing the window is now a deliberate edit to two literals, asserted literally by test_the_plate_window_is_locked_and_every_plate_is_inside_it, and a plate outside it fails -- which is the moment to decide whether the plate is wrong or the family has genuinely moved.

WHAT FINALLY WORKED FOR COBBLES, after two batches that did not: attaching the plate's OWN previous art as the reference image, rather than a written description of the camera. The three batches of five measured, ring against tile outline: 32.0/35.2 mean with a 3.3 degree mean disagreement, then 29.0/28.5 with 1.5, then 32.6/33.4 with 1.1. The winner agreed to 0.1 degrees, ring 31.5 against outline 31.6.

THE RING MEASURES, IT DOES NOT STEER. Within a batch the ring's own angle is tight -- standard deviations of 0.49, 0.68 and 1.4 degrees across the three -- but between batches it moved 3 degrees on briefs asking for the same number. The generator appears to pick a camera per session and hold it, so the ring tells you whether a batch is usable and does not make it so. Expect to run more than one batch.

`default` is flagstones_grey. It was cobbles_oval, back when that was the one plate drawn from the wrong camera; it stays flagstones_grey because a fallback should point at a plate in use, and no duty stands on cobbles_oval yet.
lift_note:
How far the ground sits ABOVE the floor line, in real pixels, positive upward -- the same on all nine tiles. Set with the `lift` slider in the placement sheet's wheel view and drawn by the sow from this value.

It is not a plate's `anchor` and the two are easy to confuse. Anchor says where down a plate's own ink the standing line falls: a fact about that piece of art, measured from it, and different for every plate. Lift says how far the whole ground sits off the floor line on the tile: a fact about the tile's layout, the same for every plate, and tuned against the parchment underneath. Move a plate up with its anchor and you have told the tool the picture is wrong; move it with the lift and you have told it the board is.

One number rather than nine because the reason to lift is the banner, and every tile has the same banner geometry. The sheet reports the clearance on the WORST plate in use, not the one under the tile you clicked -- lifting until the tile in front of you is clear while another duty's taller plate still overlaps is the failure this is meant to prevent.

Real pixels, like spread, set-back, rank gap and frame.drop, because the plate is sized in frame space (`scale` is a percentage of the frame's width) and the frame is real pixels. The banner is NOT: it scales with the cell, so the clearance the sheet reports moves with the window while the lift does not.
camera_note:
A PLATE MAY CARRY ITS OWN CAMERA under `grounds.<name>.camera`, and most do not. A round rimmed plate's outline IS an ellipse, so ground_ellipse measures it directly and nothing needs recording. A ragged patch is not an ellipse, and the fit is a best guess at a shape that has none -- so where a plate was generated with a measuring ring, the ring's reading is recorded here and the asset page reports it as that plate's angle.

The measured outline is still shown beside it and is never replaced. A recorded number is exactly the kind of thing that rots: the ring is stripped when art is filed, so nothing in the repository can re-derive it. Two tests guard it. One refuses a recorded camera further than 1.5 degrees from the plate's own outline -- that is the same bar a candidate's ring and outline must agree within, and a plate failing it should never have been filed. The other refuses a recorded camera that does not say where it came from.

planks_rough is the first and so far only plate with one.
